summary.headline: Puravankara Q2 FY27 presales rose 109% YoY to INR2,762 crores, with net debt cut by INR470 crores to INR2,366 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 presales were INR2,762 crores (up 109% YoY) on 2.38 million sq ft, with average realisation up 32% to INR11,607 per sq ft. Revenue from operations rose to INR1,033 crores (vs INR644 crores) and PAT was INR82 crores, helped by an INR149 crores exceptional gain from the Purva Zentech exit. Customer collections grew 24% to INR1,301 crores, and net debt fell to INR2,366 crores, with net debt-to-equity at 1.26x. Management says collections from the large new launches will follow as construction milestones are hit, and that the launch pipeline remains on track for FY27 guidance of INR11,200 crores, with some South and West launches possibly slipping into FY28.

vs loss of INR42 crores in Q2 FY26; includes INR149 crores exceptional gain
vs loss of INR111 crores in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR596 crores before net interest and tax; INR413 crores after

segments.name: South (Bengaluru and Kochi)
segments.commentary: Bengaluru is a major contributor to presales; Equinox 6 (part of a 6,000-unit Bengaluru complex) is selling well. Winworth-3 in Kochi expected to get RERA within days, with a launch in Q2. Grand Hills and Kanakapura Road approvals are progressing toward Q3/Q4 launches.

segments.name: West (Mumbai and Pune) and Commercial
segments.commentary: Purva Heritage sold about 30% at launch. Miami (ultra-luxury, Mumbai) got RERA in August, with transactions at around INR1.55 lakh per sq ft and 3 transactions during construction. Pali Hill RERA expected around 20 November. Deonar Baug and Cuffe Parade targeted for Q4, with Cuffe Parade possibly slipping to April-May 2027.

segments.name: Commercial assets
segments.commentary: Purva Zentech office space of about 5.46 lakh sq ft monetised for INR626 crores (exit completed in September, booked as exceptional item). Purva Aerocity is OC-received and in leasing, with 100% leasing targeted in 6-8 months; Hebbal (Bengaluru) is a new annuity asset.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales guidance maintained at INR11,200 crores, including commercial sales of about INR650 crores; H1 achieved about INR4,200 crores (37.5%), and management says it has crossed INR4,000 crores including the Zentech exit.
FY27 collection guidance of about INR6,000 crores; operating surplus expected to exceed INR1,000 crores for the year.
Planned launches of INR21,000-22,000 crores GDV; management expects at least INR15,000-16,000 crores to launch in FY27, with some projects slipping to FY28.

Business development of INR14,000-16,000 crores GDV in FY27 (Mandur INR2,300 crores, Sanna Ammanikere INR800 crores, Southeast Bengaluru INR1,100 crores, Doddagubbi and Sarjapur over INR1,000 crores each), targeting about INR15,000 crores in total.

Aerocity and Hebbal expected to generate annual rentals of about INR330 crores once fully leased; Hebbal needs about INR700 crores of construction capex and Aerocity phase 2 about INR450 crores, roughly INR1,150 crores over four years.
Expected Zentech deferred consideration of INR57-60 crores, to be received over this and next quarter.
Commercial surplus estimate of INR1,600-1,700 crores for Aerocity, based on INR65 per sq ft rent and a 7.75% cap rate.
risks_watch: Launch slippage: Cuffe Parade may move to April-May 2027, and some South projects may move to FY28. Launches needed to hit INR11,200 crores are subject to RERA and approvals.
Collection lag: large new projects (Northern Light, Estrella) must hit construction milestones before billing and collections, so collections may trail presales.
Quality of earnings: Q2 PAT includes a INR149 crores exceptional gain from the Zentech exit; reported EBITDA margin of ~27% vs project-level ~30%.
Mumbai mid/lower segment (below INR2 crore) is slower than the above INR5 crore segment; West Asia conflict cited as a medium-term risk.
Execution of new Greater Noida (NCR), Goregaon and Hebbal projects; Hebbal needs about INR700 crores of construction capex, and Aerocity phase 2 about INR450 crores.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on sales momentum, demand and the launch pipeline, but measured on timelines: several approvals are described as "subject to" RERA, with some launches possibly slipping. The CFO was more defensive on the EBITDA margin gap and on how the exceptional item should be read.
key_quotes: The central message this quarter is that stronger sales are being accompanied by better collection, faster customer handovers and a meaningful reduction in net debt.
So even if there is a shrinkage of 5% or 10% in the total demand across the country, I don't think that we will get affected by that.
Debt reduction is a choice, right?
Otherwise it's like any other project we have sold.

qa_highlights.question: Deepak Purswani asked what share of inventory was sold in the Westend and Equinox launches, how Miami sales momentum should be read, and how confident management is on the H2-weighted launch pipeline versus the INR11,200 crore guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Mallanna Sasalu said Purva Heritage sold about 30% at launch and Equinox 6 sold well; Rajat Rastogi said Miami got RERA in August with transactions near INR1.55 lakh per sq ft. Management cited Winworth-3 (Kochi) RERA within days, Grand Hills Q4, Pali Hill RERA around 20 November, Deonar Baug Q4, and Cuffe Parade possibly slipping to April-May 2027; some South projects may move to next year, but guidance was described as intact, with INR4,000 crore-plus achieved including Zentech.

qa_highlights.question: Deepak Purswani asked why residential collections grew about 25% against about 46% presales growth, and what the full-year collection and operating surplus outlook is.
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gautam said collections will follow on large new launches (Northern Light, Estrella) once construction milestones are hit and billing begins. Full-year guidance: collections about INR6,000 crores and operating surplus above INR1,000 crores; Q2 surplus includes some Zentech collections.

qa_highlights.question: Deepak Purswani asked how net debt should be expected to move by year-end, and Sarthak Jain asked how Zentech proceeds were used.
qa_highlights.answer: Mallanna Sasalu said debt reduction is a choice that depends on business development opportunities, with the aim to reduce debt where possible. Neeraj Gautam said INR250 crores of debt against Purva Zentech was repaid, other loans were repaid, and the balance went to working capital; net debt fell INR470 crores despite new land acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Singh asked for the assumptions behind the INR1,600-1,700 crore commercial surplus and the expected leasing timeline and rental income.
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gautam said the estimate relates only to Purva Aerocity, capitalised at INR65 per sq ft rent and a 7.75% cap rate. Rajat Rastogi said 100% leasing is targeted in about 6-8 months, with annual rentals of about INR330 crores from Aerocity and Hebbal once fully leased.

qa_highlights.question: Deepak Purswani asked why H1 EBITDA margin appears at 15-16% and how the reported margin relates to the project-level margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gautam said the weighted average project-level EBITDA margin is around 30%, while reported margin is 25-27% (Q2 about 27%). He said the Zentech gain is classed as exceptional under accounting rules, and that other expenses rose on approval, rates and taxes, and marketing costs ahead of 12 South and 4 West launches.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Singh asked what drove Q2 presales growth and how much of the launch pipeline falls in H2 FY27 versus FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: Mallanna Sasalu attributed growth to land acquisitions, launches, and sustenance sales in Bengaluru and Mumbai. He said INR21,000-22,000 crores of launches are planned, with at least INR15,000-16,000 crores expected in FY27 and the rest moving to FY28.

capex_capacity: Aerocity (OC received, leasing): about 95% of capex already spent; 5-7% remaining, linked to capital items and leasing; no major capex needed.
Hebbal (Bengaluru, new annuity asset): land fully paid or provided for; about INR700 crores construction capex for about 1.3 million sq ft.
Aerocity phase 2 (about 9 lakh sq ft): about INR450 crores capex; combined Hebbal and Aerocity phase 2 about INR1,150 crores over next 4 years.
Aerocity and Hebbal expected annual rentals of about INR330 crores once 100% ready and leased; Aerocity leasing targeted at 100% in 6-8 months; both assets held for annuity, not for sale.
Planned launch program of 14.5 million sq ft with estimated GDV of about INR22,600 crores, subject to approvals and launch readiness; ongoing portfolio of 33.61 million sq ft at end-September.
demand_pricing: Q2 presales INR2,762 crores on 2.38 million sq ft; average realisation up 32% YoY to INR11,607 per sq ft; H1 sales (incl. Zentech) about INR4,200 crores, 37.5% of FY27 guidance of INR11,200 crores.
Purva Heritage (West) sold about 30% at launch; Equinox 6 (6,000-unit Bengaluru complex) selling well with sustenance plus new towers.
Miami (ultra-luxury, Mumbai) got RERA in August; transactions around INR1.55 lakh per sq ft; about 3 transactions during construction in Aug-Sep.

Management cited job generation, record office leasing and record car sales as demand drivers in South; said a 5-10% national demand shrinkage would not materially affect the company. Mumbai sub-INR2 crore segment is slower than above INR5 crore segment; West Asia conflict cited as medium-term risk.
Margins: Mumbai redevelopment margins about 30% in South Mumbai and 22-25% in suburbs; greenfield MMR margins 22-30%; new land deals underwritten at gross profit above 25% (about 20% for JDA deals).

adds.what: Hebbal annuity asset, about 1.3 million sq ft construction (INR700 crore capex)
Aerocity phase 2, about 9 lakh sq ft (INR450 crore capex)

growth.why: FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crore held, with H1 at about 37.5% (INR4,200 crore incl. Zentech exit), and launches of INR15,000-16,000 crore guided, partly backed by named projects and Q2 presales up 109%, though some launches may slip to FY28 and Hebbal/Aerocity phase 2 capex (about INR1,150 crore) is a 4-year annuity build.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Project-level EBITDA margin is around 30% vs reported 25-27% (Q2 about 27%), with the gap from approval, rate and tax costs and marketing ahead of 12 South and 4 West launches; new land is underwritten at gross profit above 25%, so reported margin could widen as the gap closes, but no firm guidance was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hebbal (about 1.3 million sq ft, INR700 crore construction capex) and Aerocity phase 2 (about 9 lakh sq ft, INR450 crore capex) are planned, and the launch programme of 14.5 million sq ft (about INR22,600 crore GDV) is subject to approvals, with some South and West launches possibly slipping to FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 presales rose 109% YoY to INR2,762 crore on 2.38 million sq ft, H1 sales reached about 37.5% of the INR11,200 crore FY27 guidance, and at least INR15,000-16,000 crore of launches are guided for FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Hebbal and Aerocity phase 2 capex of about INR1,150 crore over four years is already planned, and business development of INR14,000-16,000 crore GDV is targeted for FY27, implying fresh commitments.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crore was only held, not raised, with H1 at about 37.5% and some launches (Cuffe Parade, South projects) possibly slipping to FY28.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management says some South launches may move to FY28 and Cuffe Parade to April-May 2027, and launches needed to hit guidance depend on RERA and approvals, though management says guidance is intact at over INR4,000 crore achieved including Zentech.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Winworth-3 (Kochi) launch in Q2, Grand Hills and Deonar Baug in Q4, Pali Hill RERA around 20 November, and Northern Light and Estrella follow after construction milestones.

rows.label: Net debt reduction
rows.why: Net debt fell INR470 crore to INR2,366 crore (1.26x net debt-to-equity) with INR250 crore of Zentech-linked debt repaid, but management said further reduction depends on business development opportunities.

rows.label: Collections ramp to INR6,000 crore
rows.why: H1 collections were INR2,500 crore (+31% YoY), so FY27 guidance of about INR6,000 crore implies H2 of about INR3,500 crore, which depends on large new launches hitting construction milestones.

rows.label: Aerocity leasing and Hebbal rentals
rows.why: Aerocity is targeted at 100% leasing in 6-8 months, with annual rentals of about INR330 crore from Aerocity and Hebbal once fully leased.

tone.note: Management was confident on presales momentum, demand and FY27 guidance held at INR11,200 crore, but cautious on timelines with several approvals 'subject to' RERA; analysts probed the collections lag versus presales, the reported vs project-level EBITDA margin gap, and the quality of earnings given
